notesStmt.note: Whitman included this poem in at least three different proof sheets for a cluster of poems that he attempted to publish in late 1890, so this. On the top half of the leaf is a letter to Whitman dated June 4, 1890, meaning that the draft dates from sometime after that date but before December 17, 1890, when he submitted the poem, along with three others, to Scribner's magazine, where it was rejected for publication.
A draft of the poem "For Us Two, Reader Dear," which was first published in Good-Bye My Fancy in 1891.

lg.l:
Simple, spontaneous, curious, two souls in-
terchanging,interchanging,

With the original testimony ‸for us, two continued
on to the very last.
